note: Literature reports dysmorphic facial features in over half of affected individuals (8/14) but explicitly notes the lack of a consistent or recognizable facial gestalt.

evidence.text: In a cohort of individuals with pathogenic DHX9 variants, dysmorphic features were documented in 8 of 14 assessed individuals, with the authors noting neither a consistent facial gestalt nor a recognizable pattern of human malformations.

source.title: Monoallelic variation in DHX9, the gene encoding the DExH-box helicase DHX9, underlies neurodevelopment disorders and Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease
